title: Detection of interstellar cyanamide (NH<inline-formula id="IEq1"><mml:math><mml:msub><mml:mrow></mml:mrow><mml:mn>2</mml:mn></mml:msub></mml:math></inline-formula>CN) towards the hot molecular core G10.47<inline-formula id="IEq2"><mml:math><mml:mo>+</mml:mo></mml:math></inline-formula>0.03
question: Search for and characterize the emission lines of cyanamide (NH2CN) towards the hot molecular core G10.47+0.03.

evidence.quote: In ISM, G10.47+0.03 (hereafter, G10) is a highly chemically rich HMC that was located at a distance of 8.6 kpc (cite: san14).

what.value: Column density of H2 towards G10, N(H2) = 1.3x10^23 cm^-2

evidence.quote: The estimated fractional abundance of NH$_{2}$CN with respect to H$_{2}$ was $f$(NH$_{2}$CN) = 5.076$\times$10$^{-8}$ where column density of H$_{2}$ was $N$(H$_{2}$) = 1.3$\times$10$^{23}$ cm$^{-2}$ (cite: suz16).

what.value: Column density of NH2CHO towards G10 of 3.88x10^16 cm^-2

evidence.quote: The column density of NH$_{2}$CHO towards the G10 was 3.88$\times$10$^{16}$ cm$^{-2}$ (cite: gor20).

what.value: Three-phase warm-up chemical model abundances of NH2CN

evidence.quote: Notes: a – Values taken from Table 8 of (cite: gar13);

recipe.goal: Calibrate raw interferometric data, subtract continuum, and image continuum and spectral cubes
recipe.method: Standard ALMA pipeline calibration in CASA 5.4.1 with Perley-Butler 2017 flux scaling via SETJY, target splitting via MSTRANSFORM, first-order UV continuum subtraction via UVCONTSUB, spectral cube and continuum imaging via TCLEAN, self-calibration via GAINCAL and APPLYCAL, and primary beam correction via IMPBCOR.
assumptions: Perley-Butler 2017 flux calibrator scale with 5% accuracy

recipe.method: 2D Gaussian fitting over the 1.87 mm (159.92 GHz) continuum image using CASA task IMFIT.

recipe.goal: Extract spectra, identify NH2CN transitions, and fit Gaussian line profiles
recipe.method: Extract spectrum from a 2.5" diameter circular aperture centered at RA=18h08m38.232s, Dec=-19d51m50.440s; identify NH2CN transitions using CASSIS with CDMS/JPL databases; fit Gaussian models over observed transitions in CASSIS.
key_parameters: 2.5" diameter circular region at RA (J2000) = 18h08m38.232s, Dec (J2000) = -19d51'50.440"

recipe.goal: Create integrated intensity maps and measure deconvolved emitting region sizes
recipe.method: Integrate spectral cubes over the velocity range of unblended NH2CN lines using CASA task IMMOMENTS, fit 2D Gaussians using IMFIT, and compute deconvolved source sizes.

recipe.goal: Derive NH2CN column density, rotational temperature, and fractional abundance via rotational diagram analysis
recipe.method: Perform linear rotational diagram fitting on unblended, optically thin NH2CN transitions under LTE assumptions, and compute fractional abundance relative to H2 and abundance ratio relative to NH2CHO.
key_parameters: Unblended and optically thin transitions only (excluded optically thick J = 8(7,1)-7(7,0), V = 1 transition)
assumptions: Optically thin emission and Local Thermal Equilibrium (LTE), justified by inner core density ~ 7x10^7 cm^-3

answer_key.quantity: 1.87 mm (159.92 GHz) continuum peak flux density

evidence.quote: After the generation of the continuum emission map, we fitted the 2D Gaussian over the continuum image using CASA task `IMFIT` and we obtained the peak flux 1.912$\pm$0.01 Jy beam$^{-1}$ and integrated flux 2.498$\pm$0.03 Jy.

answer_key.quantity: 1.87 mm (159.92 GHz) continuum integrated flux density

evidence.quote: After the generation of the continuum emission map, we fitted the 2D Gaussian over the continuum image using CASA task `IMFIT` and we obtained the peak flux 1.912$\pm$0.01 Jy beam$^{-1}$ and integrated flux 2.498$\pm$0.03 Jy.
The systematic velocity ($V_{LSR}$) of the sub-millimeter spectra of G10 was $\sim$68.50 km s$^{-1}$.

answer_key.quantity: Number of detected rotational transition lines of NH2CN

evidence.quote: We detected a total of nineteen rotational transition lines of NH$_{2}$CN between the frequency range of 158.49–160.43 GHz towards the G10.

answer_key.quantity: Deconvolved emitting region size of NH2CN (range across unblended transitions)

evidence.quote: The emitting region of NH$_{2}$CN was varies between 1.038$^{\prime\prime}$–1.279$^{\prime\prime}$.

Using the rotational diagram analysis, we estimated the column density of  NH$_{2}$CN was $N$(NH$_{2}$CN) = (6.60$\pm$0.1)$\times$10$^{15}$ cm$^{-2}$ with rotational temperature $T_{rot}$ = 201.20$\pm$3.3 K.

Using the rotational diagram analysis, we estimated the column density of  NH$_{2}$CN was $N$(NH$_{2}$CN) = (6.60$\pm$0.1)$\times$10$^{15}$ cm$^{-2}$ with rotational temperature $T_{rot}$ = 201.20$\pm$3.3 K.

answer_key.quantity: Fractional abundance of NH2CN with respect to H2, f(NH2CN)

evidence.quote: The estimated fractional abundance of NH$_{2}$CN with respect to H$_{2}$ was $f$(NH$_{2}$CN) = 5.076$\times$10$^{-8}$ where column density of H$_{2}$ was $N$(H$_{2}$) = 1.3$\times$10$^{23}$ cm$^{-2}$ (cite: suz16).

We also calculated that the NH$_{2}$CN/NH$_{2}$CHO abundance ratio towards the G10 was 0.170, which agreed well with the NH$_{2}$CN/NH$_{2}$CHO ratios of the low mass star-formation region IRAS 16293 B and the hot core Sgr B2 (M).
